title: IBM has released Granite Switch 4.1, two open language models that bundle a safety checker, a decision tool and a speech-to-text encoder into one endpoint.
key_facts: IBM announced Granite Switch 4.1 on 15 Oct 2026: 8B and 30B models
Each combines a base model, a decision adapter, the guardian-core safety adapter and Granite Speech 5.0 TurboCTC (470M parameters)
Apache 2.0 licence; 128K context window; model cards list 14 Oct release
IBM says all parts need roughly the same GPU memory as the base model alone
IBM says guardian-core outperforms several closed decision models on safety tasks (IBM's comparison)
Limits: speech works only in English; lowercase unpunctuated transcripts; mistranscription can change responses
quote_evidence: IBM announced Granite Switch 4.1 on October 15, 2026, releasing two modular language models, at 8 billion and 30 billion parameters, that compose a base model, a general-purpose decision adapter, a safety adapter, and an embedded speech-to-text encoder into a single hosted endpoint.
IBM says all three technologies, together with the base model, require roughly the same GPU memory as the base model by itself.
The speech cascade works only in English and returns lowercase, unpunctuated transcripts with no decode-time steering
why_it_matters_hint: One small open model that can check safety and transcribe speech on the same endpoint.
notes: Full text read. Comparisons are IBM's own.
